note: The engine release this desktop package carries. It is unpinned: no engine release publishes fermix_app_engine_linux_<arch>.tar.gz yet, so nothing is claimed. An unpinned pin is not buildable, which is the change schema 2 brings: one package carries the engine, so no pin means no engine and scripts/build_packages.sh refuses rather than producing a package with a hole in it. To pin it, take the engine tag whose release publishes fermix_app_engine_linux_x86_64.tar.gz and fermix_app_engine_linux_aarch64.tar.gz and change, all together: tag (vX.Y.Z), engine_version (the tag without its v), source_commit (the 40-character commit that tag was built from), certificate_identity (https://github.com/tezra-io/fermix/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/ plus the tag), and each artifact's asset and sha256 (the digest in the asset's .sha256 sidecar). Either every one of those is null or every one is filled: scripts/engine_pin.sh refuses a half-filled pin, which is the dangerous state because it reads as a pin to a glance and names an engine nothing can verify. The pinned engine version is also this desktop package's own version, because one package carries both halves and they are one build.
